messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — PR #5248 adds a new streaming iterator example for Python but it's failing the docs build :grimacing:
Priya: link?
Alex: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5248
Jordan: failing because we're using a manual for-loop + time.sleep in the snippet. linter flags blocking IO in async examples.
Alex: yeah, we should switch to the async generator pattern and use the SDK retry helper. also sync up the TS/Go examples so they show the same cursor + retry surface.
Kai: i can do the TS snippet. want it to show cursor-based pagination + exponential backoff + jitter. keep it tiny.
Alex: ideal Python pattern i had in mind:
```python
async def stream_responses(client, prompt):
    async for chunk in client.responses.stream({"prompt": prompt}):
        print(chunk.text, end="")

# wrap with client.utils.retry_async for transient errors
```
Priya: can we use the SDK's built-in retry helper instead of tenacity? keeps the example dependency-free and easier to copy-paste.
Jordan: yes — there's client.utils.retry_async (public helper). it's already used in a couple internal examples.
Alex: sweet. I'll update the PR to use client.utils.retry_async and add one-line comment about preserving cursor tokens for resume scenarios.
Kai: TS version idea:
```ts
for await (const part of client.responses.stream({prompt})) {
  process.stdout.write(part.text)
}
// show how to store resume_token from final message
```
Priya: pushed a tiny CI tweak to the docs workflow to ignore network checks for code-blocks (network=false). should unblock the lint false positives for snippets.
Alex: i'll push changes in ~30m. @Jordan @Kai please review once i mark ready-for-review :thumbsup:
DocsBot: Build queued for branch alex/stream-snippet (job #3423)
Kai: will review TS + changelog once tests pass.
Jordan: added a very short migration note for users moving from cursor-pagination v1 -> v2 inside the examples folder. keeps backward compatibility section minimal.
Alex: thanks y'all — if CI green i'll merge and then follow up with a docs-site patch to render the snippets with the new helper examples :tada:
